messages:
Alex: Heads-up — incoming support ticket from AcmeCorp: high rate of KMS decrypt failures after a recent key rotation. Customer reports many API 403s and a subset of requests ended up in our DLQ. They included repro. Pinging eng-security for triage.

Morgan: Do we have the original logs + the exact KMS key ARN + the encryption context they sent? 403s usually mean encryption context mismatch or missing grants.

Alex: Paste from customer (redacted) — they show AccessDenied from KMS and a proxy log with a truncated header.
```
ERROR: kms.Decrypt AccessDeniedException: The request was rejected because the provided encryption context does not match.
KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
Request headers: X-Encryption-Context: eyJwcm9qZWN0X2lkIjoiYWNtZS1wcm9qZWN0Iiwi...<truncated>
Proxy response: 403 from KMS
Retries: client retried 3x then DLQ
```

Raj: Two things to check: 1) Are we preserving the full encryption context end-to-end? 2) Any intermediate proxy/ALB/nginx with header size limits that might be chopping the base64? Also confirm whether the rotation produced a new keyId that customer pinned.

Sam: I pulled CloudTrail for that key ARN. We see Decrypt calls around the time, but ~12% of them show KMS returning AccessDenied and there are no corresponding CloudTrail entries for our agent requests that went to DLQ (looks like the proxy blocked them before the KMS client call).

Alex: Customer says they encode the encryption context as a JSON then base64 into X-Encrypt-Ctx header. Some of their contexts are large (many labels). Suspect header length + ALB/nginx trimming. Repro steps from customer below:
```
# repro (customer)
ENCCTX=$(echo -n '{"project_id":"acme-project","files":[...very long list...]}' | base64)
curl -H "X-Encrypt-Ctx: $ENCCTX" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/decrypt
# result: 403 + body: {"error":"decrypt_failed"}
```

Morgan: That matches earlier oddities. If header is trimmed, the base64 decodes to malformed JSON -> encryption context mismatch -> KMS AccessDenied. Two concurrent impacts: 1) failed decrypts, 2) clients retrying rapidly causing bill-inflation and DLQ noise.

Raj: Quick checks: which component validates header length? Eng-platform (edge/nginx) has a default header buffer of 8k; ALB has 16k total for headers. If customer's encoded payload crossed that, it could be truncated. Also we should check our KMS client library behavior when encctx is malformed (do we call Decrypt at all?).

Sam: I instrumented the proxy logs: several requests had "truncated" field logged by our edge microproxy. Those requests never hit the KMS client — our handler returns 403 early if encctx fails JSON decoding. That explains missing CloudTrail entries.

Alex: Impact summary for support ticket: customer saw ~600 failed decrypts over 2 hours, billing spike from retries + DLQ reprocessing, and they requested audit evidence of decrypt attempts (some are missing in CloudTrail because we never reached KMS).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3248. Pager duty escalation notified to oncall SRE. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-3248

oncall-bot: Severity: P2. Customer-facing mitigation requested.

Morgan: Short-term mitigation options:
- Ask AcmeCorp to reduce encryption context size (quickest customer-side fix).
- Add server-side validation that returns 4xx with clear message before DLQ and avoid retries (prevents billing spike).
- Temporarily relax edge buffer trimming (risky) or configure to allow larger headers for that route.

Raj: Long-term:
- Support passing encryption context in request body (safer for large contexts) and mark header-encctx deprecated.
- Add instrumentation that records when encctx is malformed + a synthetic CloudTrail-like audit row so customers have traceability even if we fail pre-KMS.

Sam: Repro steps I ran in staging: sent a 20KB base64 encctx and saw edge trim -> handler JSON decode fails -> 403 returned without KMS call. Patch idea: return 400 with body: {"error":"encryption_context_truncated"} so client can debug immediately. I can make a small handler change and ship to staging.

Alex: Can you also capture the raw header bytes (redact) for the tickets? Customer wants proof of truncation. If we can show "truncation marker" in our proxy logs it helps support + compliance.

Morgan: I'll coordinate with Support to notify AcmeCorp: propose immediate guidance (reduce encctx, sinkretries) and let them know we're deploying a clearer 400 response in staging in ~2hrs. Also will open a private postmortem to cover audit gap and billing impact.

Raj: Permissions check item: ensure that if such malformed requests are forwarded to KMS accidentally, our KMS key policies and grants are still correctly scoped. Not seeing any grant errors right now, but worth adding to checklist.

Alex: Action items:
- Sam: quick handler patch to return 400 + log raw header (sanitized) -> staging (ETA 2h).
- Morgan: customer comms + support runbook update (ETA 1h).
- Raj: add audit fallback plan and policy checklist (ETA EOD).
- Alex: follow up with billing to flag and cap customer's unexpected charges while we remediate.

Sam: I'll post a staging link when the build is up and include steps to reproduce.

Morgan: Thanks — keeping this thread as the single source for the ticket. Will escalate to ENG-PLATFORM if changing edge buffer needed. :pray:
